title: Frostbite: A new CPU architecture discovered, designed and verified by AI
lede: Architect Labs says its AI systems designed Frostbite, a CPU with a new instruction set built around interaction nets, taking it from compiler and ISA through RTL to final layout.

points: Interaction nets keep dependencies explicit and give each value a single owner, so parallelism comes from the program rather than out-of-order hardware.
On 25 workloads, 15 held back until the final evaluation, it reports 4.59x performance per watt against a dual-issue in-order core.
Agents specified the chip in ASL, an in-house formal language that lowers to Lean; the spec grew past 800,000 lines of Lean.
A system model was tuned against the RTL until power estimates matched within 5%, then simulated about 660x faster than RTL.
Agent swarms proposed 58 architecture changes in parallel and kept 37.

points.text: Skeptics say an in-order baseline is a weak comparison next to modern out-of-order cores, and the program set is small.
Commenters argue over credit: one says humans supplied the core ideas and AI mostly turned decades of research into a product.
Several see echoes of earlier dataflow machines, from 1980s dynamic dataflow designs to WaveScalar.
One notes the tested kernels use small, fixed working sets and asks how the design copes with programs that build large structures.
